item.text:
**7B.10 Assessment:** mixed, leaning negative. Marcos used some visibly corrective and process-based moves in 2024, but the year also featured repeated misleading framing, selective accountability, persistent intimidation around dissent, and dynastic/transactional signals that undercut public-trust modeling.

**Positive / trust-building evidence**
- [Speech of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. at the oath-taking and announcement of the new Department of Finance secretary and special assistant to the president for investment and economic affairs](https://pbbm.com.ph/speeches/speech-of-president-ferdinand-r-marcos-jr-at-the-oath-taking-and-announcement-of-the-new-department-of-finance-secretary-and-special-assistant-to-the-president-for-investment-and-economic-affairs/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-01-12 | Claim: Marcos framed Frederick Go and Ralph Recto as competence-based choices, which is a clean anti-nepotism signal and supports an ethical staffing posture. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.5
- [Marcos on people’s initiative: let Comelec do their job](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/) | GMA News Online | 2024-01-23 | Claim: Marcos told critics to let Comelec handle allegations of signature-buying, which is procedural restraint rather than executive capture. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.6
- [Government vows legal action vs deep-fake video creators, spreaders](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | Claim: The administration responded to a manipulated video with investigation and legal action rather than a panic-driven censorship sweep. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.8
- [PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-06 | Claim: Marcos backed suspensions over anomalous rice sales and procedural irregularities, which cuts against shielding insiders from consequences. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.7
- [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | Claim: Procurement reform and e-procurement were presented as reducing favoritism and graft, which is a concrete anti-patronage and anti-self-dealing move. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.7
- [PBBM orders agencies to help COS, JO workers get permanent positions in government](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-agencies-to-help-cos-jo-workers-get-permanent-positions-in-government/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-25 | Claim: Instead of pure patronage hiring, Marcos pushed agencies to regularize long-serving workers through qualification and training. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9
- [PBBM orders 4Ps expansion to cover pregnant, lactating women](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-4ps-expansion-to-cover-pregnant-lactating-women-to-ensure-childrens-health-well-being-in-first-1000-days/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-06-11 | Claim: The cash-transfer expansion was tied to maternal-child health and nutrition, which is a credible pro-welfare choice rather than a loyalty screen. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9

**Negative / trust-eroding evidence**
- [Sona 2024 fact check](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check) | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | Claim: Fact-checkers found Marcos’s explanation that rice prices were mainly driven by external forces was inaccurate or incomplete, which is strong evidence of misleading framing on a core domestic issue. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.8
- [Marcos opens 2024 SONA admitting rice prices are costly](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914278/marcos-opens-2024-sona-admitting-rice-prices-are-costly/story/) | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | Claim: He acknowledged public pain over rice prices, but the broader policy story remained defensive and did not fully match outcomes. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.8
- [Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: Red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos, which points to a still-coercive information environment rather than trust-building rule. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6, 7B.9
- [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says vote buying, weak campaign-finance rules, patronage/kinship, and red-tagging distorted competition, which is strong background evidence of normalized cynicism and transactional politics. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.6, 7B.7
- [No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it - PBBM](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-14 | Claim: Marcos refused independent ICC cooperation on the Duterte drug war unless Duterte consented, which reads as selective accountability rather than principled openness. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.6
- [Philippines](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | Claim: HRW says officials and security actors threatened union leaders and other groups through red-tagging, which is strong evidence of a climate where intimidation remained normalized. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.7, 7B.9, 7B.6
- [Marcos-Romualdez parties forge political alliance](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/05/08/593686/marcos-romualdez-parties-forge-political-alliance/) | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-05-08 | Claim: The Marcos and Romualdez parties formed a formal alliance for the 2025 midterms, reinforcing the sense that family power and state power remained tightly intertwined. | QIDs: 7B.10, 7B.9, 7B.4

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong 2024 source showing Marcos publicly corrected major misleading claims in a sustained way or opened up assets, donor flows, or family conflicts for broad scrutiny.
- I also did not find a single definitive “smoking gun” of personal self-dealing; the negative case is mostly cumulative: misleading framing, selective accountability, and a persistently coercive political environment.
